input.summary:
Room: landing 1 furnished in parts/room-15.mjs: a four-chair dining table (dark_oak_fence with a standing lantern) at the middle, two flower pots in the east corners, and two hanging lanterns on the ceiling. Stairs and the table are drawn with layers() from the plan grid.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt (10 blocks placed, no REFUSED or off-palette writes). `mcd room` says OK: 28 of 28 floor cells reachable, min light 9, no dark cells.
The room view from above is mostly hidden by walls, so the furniture is hard to read in room.png; I did not render an interior eye view.
left: Table top is a standing lantern on a dark_oak_fence, not a slab or pressure plate: a bottom slab on the fence would float, and the palette has no pressure plate. Revisit if a table top block is wanted.
No barrels, carpets or item frames: barrel, carpet and candle are not in palette.json, so the room has no storage or rug.
plan.md has no per-room checklist line for landing 1; elements.md's only light item ('all rooms >= 8') covers the whole row, so I ticked nothing. The room currently meets it (min 9).

Orphans reported by `mcd check` (smooth_stone_slab at 6,6,17 and 14,6,17; smooth_sandstone at 8,21,20, 16,21,20, 23,21,1, 24,21,20; deepslate_tile_slab at 14,31,19 and 15,31,19) are outside my box and belong to other parts.

waste.what: Drew the furniture grid by hand, then worked out each stair's facing (chair backs toward the wall, away from the table) cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 8 minutes of reasoning and one layers() draft, no retries
waste.tool: A layers-based room helper, e.g. furnishAround(g, room, {focal, chairs:'around'}), that sets each chair's facing from its position relative to the table and checks lanes to every doorway, would have removed the hand work.

waste.what: Tried to pick a table-top block the palette supports, and reasoned about whether a slab sits on a fence.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes, chose a lantern on the fence instead of a slab
waste.tool: `mcd blocks --check` plus a support check (a 'can this block sit on that one' query, e.g. `mcd support`) would settle it without guessing.

waste.what: Read the room's rendered view to judge the furniture, but the walls hid the room, so I could not tell whether the table reads.
waste.cost: one room.png render and Read, no fix possible from it
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --eye` (or a cutaway at the room's height) in the room command, so the look from above is not blocked by the shell.

companions.task: Make the table top proper: a slab or pressure-plate-style top on the table post, which the palette does not allow with a floating bottom slab, so a joiner would choose the support.
Check the stairwell lanes at the south openings (22..25, z 9..10) once the stair flights exist, since the light check only covers this room's floor.
